title: Gabon textile samples
lede: Nathalie Du Pasquier’s screen-printed cotton Gabon: jagged shapes, checkered borders, and six colorways.
summary: Du Pasquier’s 1982 printed cotton: zigzag blocks and checkered bands in six colorways.

creator.name: Nathalie Du Pasquier (designer); produced by Rainbow, Milan

evidence.note: Downloaded the museum’s published image (843 px wide) from [the Art Institute of Chicago IIIF server](https://www.artic.edu/artworks/72939) to a private scratchpad and inspected it with the Read tool on 2026-09-25. No image is stored in the catalogue. The Met’s record of the same design was read; it has no online image.

styles.note: Du Pasquier was a Memphis member and a principal pattern designer for the group; this print shows the style’s surface language.

context: The Art Institute lists six samples of Gabon, designed by Nathalie Du Pasquier and produced by Rainbow, Milan, 1982; cotton twill, screen printed. The museum also holds her Zaire, Uganda, Kenya, Congo, Cameroon, and Zambia prints from the same year. [AIC record](https://www.artic.edu/artworks/72939).
The Met holds a full length of “Gabon” textile, 1982, cotton, 139.7 × 403.9 cm. [Met record](https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/484547).
A 1983 Memphis leaflet by Christoph Radl labels “Gabon – 1982” among the group’s patterns. See [Memphis Milano leaflet](ref:radl-memphis-milano-leaflet-1983).
observed: Large jagged polygons in red, blue, green, purple, and white overlap one another.
Thick black outlines run around the shapes, broken by small checkered segments in white, blue, and pink.
Zigzag and stepped edges appear throughout; no curve is visible in the main swatch.
Five narrower strips show the same drawing in other colorways, including orange-red, teal-brown, and blue-black.
The samples hang from a black header card printed “RAINBOW”.
interpretation: The print is dense and uses clashing colors, and its checkered outline recurs in Memphis graphics and laminates. The colorway strips show that the drawing, not a single palette, carries the identity.
borrow: Outline flat shapes with a thick band that is itself patterned, such as a checkerboard.
Design one pattern and test it in several full-saturation colorways.

rights.statement: AIC marks the object as not public domain. No image is stored.
